name: nine_thousand_torches
revision: r1 (2026-11-10): written from the critic's park note: the trading-hall answer dropped for the goodbye
caption: who put 9,000 torches on my village 🔥
logline: A villager kid wakes to find a torch on every block of his village and thinks something terrible is coming, but follows the last row to his own door, where his best friend, the village's player, places the final torch and leaves the game for good.
question: why tf is there a torch on every single block of this village?
premise: One morning a plains village wakes up with a torch on every grass block, fence post and hay bale: nine thousand of them. The villager kid who tells it knows zombies can't spawn on a lit block, so he decides something big must be coming. Milo, the player who lives in the village and his best friend, says 'see you tomorrow' every night when he logs off; yesterday Milo said his mom made him promise, one last night, which the kid reads as Milo being grounded again. This morning all of Milo's things are in the kid's family chest and Milo's house is gone, just a square of torches. One row of torches is still growing; the kid follows it to his own door.
twist: Nothing is coming: Milo is going. He is leaving the world for good (his mom's rule: one last night), so he spent the whole night spawn-proofing every block of the village, so no zombie can ever spawn in it once nobody is there to fight them. He took his own house down so it wouldn't be one dark room left behind, gave everything he owned to his best friend, and saved the friend's door for the last torch. He places it, waves, and the chat says 'Milo left the game'. He didn't say 'see you tomorrow' because it isn't true. The torches are the goodbye.

lines.text: Someone put / NINE THOUSAND / TORCHES / on my village / last NIGHT.
lines.say: Someone put nine thousand torches on my village last night.
lines.direction: one quick breath, no pause inside; amazed and bright, a lift on the number

lines.text: The GRASS. / The FENCES. / Even the HAY BALES.
lines.direction: a fast list, each item more amazed than the last, a laugh on the last one

lines.text: Zombies can't SPAWN / on a lit block. / So why / EVERY block?
lines.direction: the first half proud, he knows this rule; the question quick and puzzled
full volume, spooked and thrilled at once, eyes wide; not whispered

lines.text: My best friend / MILO / is our PLAYER.
lines.direction: proud and happy, a grin on the name

lines.text: Every night, / he says / see you TOMORROW / and logs OFF.
lines.direction: matter-of-fact and fond, quick; the quoted words said the way a friend says them

lines.text: Yesterday / Milo said, / Mom made me PROMISE. / One LAST night.
lines.say: Yesterday Milo said, "Mom made me promise. One last night."
lines.direction: telling it lightly, no weight on it at all, he doesn't get it

lines.text: This morning, / all his STUFF / was in OUR chest.
lines.direction: back to the strange morning, excited, a lift on the last word

lines.text: He's HIDING it / from whatever's COMING.
lines.direction: sure of himself, a little thrilled; full volume

lines.text: His HOUSE / was GONE. / Just a square / of TORCHES.
lines.direction: puzzled, a beat of surprise on the second phrase, not scared
quick and curious, leaning in, full volume

lines.text: I followed it / right to MY door.
lines.direction: fast, running; surprised on the last word

lines.text: Milo put / the LAST one / by my DOOR. / And WAVED.
lines.direction: happy to see him, a smile in it; the last two words simple

lines.text: He didn't say, / see you / TOMORROW.
lines.say: He didn't say, see you tomorrow. <short pause>
lines.direction: full volume, slower, the bubbles gone; plain and steady, he just understood; not whispered, not breathy

ending.loop: cause and effect: the goodbye at the door is why L01's village has nine thousand torches 'last night'; L01's 'someone' is Milo, and 'Something BIG must be COMING' (L04) turns into someone going

Dawn (23000): sky blue-grey, no sun yet, torch glow and bloom at their strongest. This is the count shot: the viewer must believe 9,000.
